Écrins massif · La Bérarde · zoom 12 · 44.915°N 6.295°E

Pick a basemap for OutThere

The same valley, rendered by eight free map styles. The pin is where one of your bivouac spots would sit. Look at how readable the terrain is, how the pin stands out, and how long you could stare at it.

Best for judging terrain

OpenTopoMap

Contour lines, shaded relief, marked hiking paths and huts. The classic hiker's look, a little busy.

Cost
Free, no key. Light use only.
Credit
CC-BY-SA, OSM + SRTM
Cleanest French option

Plan IGN

The French national mapping agency's modern style. Clean, with trails, huts, summits and spot heights.

Cost
Free, no key. France only.
Credit
IGN Géoplateforme
Most nostalgic

Cartes IGN

The look of the paper IGN hiking maps, with place names and refuges. Very familiar if you walk with the orange-and-blue sheets.

Cost
Public demo key, not guaranteed. France only.
Credit
IGN Géoplateforme
Calm and neutral

Esri World Topo

Soft, muted colours with gentle hillshading. Easy on the eye, less detail on trails.

Cost
Free for light use. Needs attribution.
Credit
Esri, USGS, NOAA
Most editorial

National Geographic

Earthy parchment tones with relief shading. Very atmospheric, with a lot of character at world scale.

Cost
Free for light use. Needs attribution.
Credit
Esri, National Geographic
Good as a second layer

Satellite

Real imagery. Useful for spotting flat ground, scree, and lakes before you commit to a bivouac.

Cost
Free for light use. Needs attribution.
Credit
Esri, Maxar
Least outdoorsy

OpenStreetMap Standard

The default web map. Familiar, but built for streets, and mountains look flat.

Cost
Free, no key. Not for heavy traffic.
Credit
OpenStreetMap contributors
Best for many pins

Light Gray Canvas

Almost no colour. The map recedes and your own pins and photos carry the page.

Cost
Free for light use. Needs attribution.
Credit
Esri

These are real tiles captured at zoom 12 over the Écrins. Zoomed out to the whole world, every style looks different again, so tell me if you want to see that too.

Not shown: vector styles such as MapTiler Outdoor or Topo, which need a free API key to render. They draw smoother and rotate and tilt, but the raster styles above are a fair guide to the overall aesthetic.
